messages:
maria_partnerships: Quick sync — drafting a compact taxonomy for SI lead claiming + escalation. Want this tight so sales/PD/eng know who owns pipeline and when to return leads. Link: https://redwood-internal/si-claim-taxonomy (draft)

alex_dev: nice. can we define a hard 'claim window' and a separate 'engagement window'? i.e., claiming is initial ownership, engagement is active pursuit.

sam_se: Agree. For bundled deals (SI + HW/cloud marketplace) who gets credit for initial opp?

maria_partnerships: Proposed rules (short):
- Claim window = 7 days after intake unless auto-assigned via partner marketplace.
- Engagement window = 90 days from claim start; if no activity for 14 days, the lead reverts to intake.
- Bundled deals: credit split rule = 60/40 in favor of the party that owns the signed PO/contract. If both sign concurrently, split based on primary billing owner.

katie_salesops: For CRM tagging, use tags: `si_claimed_by:<partner_short>`, `si_claimed_at:<ts>`, `si_escalation_level:<L1|L2>`. Example SFDC update snippet:```update Opportunity set Partner_Claim__c = 'SI-Northpoint', Partner_Claimed_At__c = '2026-03-15T12:00:00Z' where Id = '006xx0000'```

jordan_ae: who is the escalation contact for L2? last time we waited too long for a reply from partner success.

maria_partnerships: L1 = partner AE / partner success. L2 = partnership_ops (oncall rotation) -> partnership_ops@redwood.com. Escalation SLAs: L1 ack within 24h, L2 ack within 4h business hours. Emergency (deal blocks) ping: #release-war-room.

sam_se: How do we handle marketplace-sourced leads that have a different T&C or commit flow?

maria_partnerships: Marketplace-sourced leads default-claim to the marketplace owner for 48 hours to accept. If rejected/no-response, go to intake pool. If the marketplace lead involves a reserved Dedicated capacity ask, escalate to eng-sales-ops for capacity check.

alex_dev: operational question — can we add a lightweight webhook that sets `si_claimed_at` when partner accepts? partnership-bot could post to slack + update SFDC.

partnerships-bot: [automated] New webhook blueprint available: `/webhooks/si-claim/accept` — posts to #partnerships and updates Opportunity tag. See docs: https://redwood-internal/webhooks/si-claim

katie_salesops: i'll add the webhook mapping to the SFDC workflow this afternoon and create automation to re-open stale claims after 14 days.

jordan_ae: quick ask: can we carve out a special flow for strategic accounts where we freeze reversion for 30 days? some enterprise deals need longer nurture.

maria_partnerships: yes — Strategic tag (`si_strategic:true`) prevents automatic reversion. Criteria: ARR > $250k or legal/regulatory gating. We should document examples in the doc.

sam_se: is there a playbook for joint announcements and co-marketing? those often need both partner comms and product readiness checks.

maria_partnerships: added short checklist in the draft: legal sign-off, joint PR timeline, model/data residency notes, dedicated runbook for Dedicated/private customers, and a pre-announce tech-readiness call 2 weeks out.

alex_dev: small ask from eng: when a partner claims, can we tag `requires_oncall_review:true` for Dedicated/private deals so eng-oncall sees infra implications?

maria_partnerships: good call — will add `requires_oncall_review` flag to the claim form for deal-type options.

katie_salesops: i'll push the CRM field updates and sample automation by EOD. Can we get thumbs up from sales and AE leads by EOD tomorrow so we can start a 2-week pilot? :thumbsup:

jordan_ae: 👍 from me

sam_se: +1

alex_dev: +1

maria_partnerships: thanks all — i'll tidy the doc, add the webhook blueprint and escalation matrix. tagging this thread for the pilot kickoff.

partnerships-bot: [automated] Pilot kickoff scheduled: 2026-03-25 16:00 UTC. Calendar invite sent to participants.
